prompt: Explain the highest-impact everyday actions to cut household emissions.

card.oneLiner: The biggest household levers are electricity use, transport and diet, and improving them often saves money as well.
keyPoints: Efficient cooling and appliances cut the most electricity.
Shifting trips to public transport and cycling cuts fuel use.
More plant-rich meals lower diet-related emissions.
Rooftop solar can clean up remaining electricity use.

framework.name: Bureau of Energy Efficiency
framework.gloss: Standards and labels for efficient appliances.

framework.name: IPCC AR6
framework.gloss: Demand-side options with high mitigation potential.

whatYouCanDo: Pick two or three high-impact changes and sustain them.
Set your AC around 24-26°C and service it regularly.
Look into rooftop solar if you own your home.
card.caveats: Educational information, not professional advice. Impacts depend on your local grid and lifestyle.

prompt: Explain how your daily travel choices affect emissions.
hook: The vehicle and the distance both count.

card.oneLiner: Shifting trips to public transport, cycling and walking, and choosing efficient or electric vehicles, cuts transport emissions.
keyPoints: Switching a trip from car to bus or metro cuts emissions sharply.
Short trips are ideal for walking and cycling.
Higher occupancy reduces emissions per person.
Electric vehicles cut tailpipe emissions, more so on a cleaner grid.

framework.name: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
framework.gloss: Urban transport policy promoting public and active travel.

whatYouCanDo: Combine errands into a single trip.
Try public transport for one regular journey.
Consider an electric vehicle for your next purchase.
card.caveats: Educational information, not professional advice. Emissions vary with grid mix, fuel and vehicle.

sources.title: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

prompt: Explain simple ways to cut home electricity use and bills.
hook: Every unit saved is a unit not generated.

card.oneLiner: Efficient appliances, sensible cooling settings and switching off standby loads cut both bills and emissions.
keyPoints: Cooling is usually the biggest household load.
Star-labelled appliances use less for the same service.
LED lighting and efficient fans cut steady demand.
Standby loads add up across many devices.
whatYouCanDo: Set the AC to 24-26°C and use a fan alongside.
Clean AC filters and service appliances.
Switch off and unplug devices you are not using.
card.caveats: Educational information, not professional advice. Savings depend on usage patterns and climate.

prompt: Explain practical ways to reduce single-use plastic in daily life.

card.oneLiner: Carrying reusables, refusing single-use items and segregating waste keeps plastic out of landfills and oceans.
keyPoints: Refusing is easier than dealing with waste later.
Reusable bags, bottles and cutlery replace many disposables.
Clean, separated plastic is far easier to recycle.
Supporting formal recyclers improves recovery.

framework.name: Plastic Waste Management Rules
framework.gloss: Rules against single-use plastic and for producer responsibility.

framework.name: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

whatYouCanDo: Keep a reusable bag and bottle ready to go.
Say no to single-use cutlery and straws.
Segregate and clean plastic before recycling.
card.caveats: Educational information, not professional advice. Recycling infrastructure varies by city.

sources.title: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

prompt: Explain how individuals can push for larger change beyond personal habits.
hook: Personal action is necessary, not sufficient.

card.oneLiner: Beyond personal habits, citizens can shape change through civic participation, local bodies and holding institutions accountable.
keyPoints: Local governments control much of waste, water and transport.
Meetings and consultations are open to residents.
Collective action at work and school amplifies impact.
Transparency tools help citizens press for action.

framework.name: Mission LiFE
framework.gloss: National initiative linking individual and community action.

framework.name: UN Environment Programme
framework.gloss: Global platform on individual and collective action.

whatYouCanDo: Attend a local body meeting on waste or transport.
Join or start a residents' group on a local issue.
Push your workplace or school to cut emissions.
card.caveats: Educational information, not professional advice. Civic channels differ by place; be patient and persistent.
